verdict: 2026-07-29 11:20:58 PDT — The purpose shape is sound: README is canonical and ARCHITECTURE points to it while recording architectural consequences. However, I would not ship the roadmap or linter in their current shapes: ROADMAP recreates shadow lifecycle state, and the linter can pass on incidental name occurrences.

findings.title: ROADMAP is still a hand-maintained status dashboard
findings.claim: The roadmap re-asserts mutable lifecycle facts—“stable,” “shipped,” “staged,” “in-flight,” “parked,” “being rebuilt,” and a curated list of “open work”—despite DR-1 assigning those facts to git, BACKLOG, and story files. Links do not remove the duplication when the surrounding prose copies current status. This recreates the second-writer state model the story exists to prevent.
findings.alternative: Retain only durable strategic direction and unresolved choices: the lightweight-loop direction, reviewer diversification, and deep-audit core/plugin/park decision. Remove lifecycle labels, delivery narratives, and the curated open-work inventory; link once to README/git, BACKLOG, and relevant stories for current state and history.
findings.win: Removes roughly 15–20 lines of shadow status and eliminates the obligation to update ROADMAP whenever a merge, OPS item, or story changes state.

findings.title: The linter checks incidental substrings, not documented skills
findings.claim: Inventory extraction greps the whole install script rather than the ARTIFACTS block, while coverage accepts any occurrence of the bare skill name. A deployed skill named `audit`, for example, would already pass both document checks through unrelated prose without a `/audit` feature entry; an example or comment outside ARTIFACTS could also create a phantom skill. The gate therefore does not reliably enforce its sole invariant.
findings.alternative: Restrict extraction to quoted records inside the ARTIFACTS array—or expose a read-only artifact-listing mode from install.sh—and require an exact structural command token such as backticked `/name` with delimiters in both documents. This pins command identity, not prose wording.
findings.win: Eliminates both false-green paths while retaining the minimal, phrase-independent check; a generically named deployed command can no longer pass through incidental mentions.
